column3: “Knew” preserves the intimate knowing image of “had relations”; “I have acquired a man with the LORD” preserves the acquisition wording without explicitly adding “the help of.”
“From their fat” names fat explicitly, rather than the broader “best portions.”
“Lifting up” preserves the image rendered “be accepted”; “if you do not do well” does not add an explicit refusal.
Cain speaks to his brother, but the direct quotation “Let us go out to the field” is not expressed in the Hebrew wording used here.
The speaker is only “He,” without an explicit repeated “the LORD.”
“Cursed from the ground” does not express a separate verb “banished.”
“Therefore” preserves the linking word instead of the reply “Not so!”
“He was building a city” preserves the continuing construction rather than a completed “built a city.”
“For” preserves the explanatory conjunction rather than the conditional “if.”
